answer: A verifier enforces identity by demanding 1,000 units of recursive proofs as a scarce resource, where honest agents commit work to a vertex before selection. If a karst-like audit detects divergent history from cloned agents, the system triggers a permanent burn. Each identity costs work; 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times the cost of one honest node. If an agent shares a willow-branch trace of memory, the fault locks assets.
